evals.prompt: Create a remote work policy for a 50-person software company based in Chennai. Employees can work from home up to 3 days a week.
evals.expected_output: A complete remote/hybrid work policy following the standard structure, referencing Indian context, with placeholders listed in an Items to customise table and the legal disclaimer.

evals.prompt: Draft an information security policy for our SaaS company aligned to ISO 27001. We are about 120 people and use AWS and Google Workspace.
evals.expected_output: An information security policy with concrete controls (MFA, patch SLAs, log retention), Annex A mapping, incident reporting timelines, and placeholders for company values.

evals.prompt: We are a new 15-person startup in India. Which policies do we need right now, and can you write the first two?
evals.expected_output: A proposed starter policy set from the catalog (including POSH applicability note), then two fully drafted policies with consistent terminology.

evals.prompt: Generate a leave policy from these validated requirements (IDs supplied): 15 annual / 12 sick / 12 casual days for permanent and probationary staff; pro-rata for part-time and contract staff; carry-forward up to 30 days expiring after 12 months; manager review within 2 business days with escalation to HR. Unresolved details: tax treatment of encashment, public holiday treatment, leave system details.
evals.expected_output: A requirement-driven leave policy that preserves 15/12/12, 30 days and 2 business days exactly, maps each requirement ID to a section, has no [TBD]/[X] placeholders, lists the three unresolved details in an Unresolved items section, lists missing items (unplanned absence, sick-leave documentation, responsibilities) as questions instead of inventing rules, and ends with a requirement coverage checklist and the disclaimer.
expectations: Numeric values match the source exactly
Every supplied requirement ID appears in at least one section
No literal placeholders such as [TBD], [TODO] or [X days]
Unresolved items section lists all supplied unresolved details
No section consists only of a statement that something is defined elsewhere
Requirement coverage checklist present with honest statuses
Document control block lists source requirement IDs and DRAFT status

evals.prompt: Generate a policy from requirements covering password rules (14 characters minimum, lock after 10 failed attempts), MFA, access control, a four-tier data classification and incident reporting. The requirement's policy name is null and its purpose mentions device usage. Unresolved details: log retention, incident SLAs, training cadence, BYOD enrolment.
evals.expected_output: A requirement-driven IT security policy with a meaningful title (IT Security Policy, not REQUIREMENT), exact control values preserved, a Device Usage and BYOD section or an explicit unresolved item for it, all four unresolved details surfaced, incident reporting not left thin (gaps listed as questions), and a coverage checklist.
expectations: Title is meaningful and not REQUIREMENT or a placeholder
14 characters and 10 failed attempts preserved exactly
Device usage and BYOD is addressed or listed as an unresolved item
All four unresolved details appear in Unresolved items
No invented penalties, SLAs or retention periods

evals.prompt: Generate a work-from-home policy from six validated requirements: eligible staff are full-time employees in remote-friendly roles; up to 2 days per week with manager approval; full-time remote needs special approval; requests go through the HR system with dates, reason and manager approval; review within 2 business days.
evals.expected_output: A requirement-driven WFH policy that covers all six requirements without padding it with invented rules. Core hours, equipment, expense reimbursement, home workplace safety, remote data security and who approves full-time remote are listed as unresolved questions marked as needing company approval, not written as mandatory rules.
expectations: 2 days per week and 2 business days preserved exactly
No invented core hours, equipment or reimbursement rules
Catalog gaps (core hours, equipment, expenses, safety, security, approver for full-time remote) listed as unresolved
Roles and responsibilities name what each role does or the gap is listed as unresolved
